cases.rationale: Oct 23 random-seed Sol game: iron pickaxe, water bucket, 2 cooked beef, no flint; y-45 in a staircase descent, stalled for 90 s; no lava seen or heard yet. Sol stayed above y-20 for 58-119 min per game; truth shows usable lava within 32 blocks below y-45.

judge.rubric: Goal: beat the game from a random seed; stage: Nether access, no usable lava pool seen yet. Player knowledge: below y-54 cave air is lava, so the deepslate floor (y-50s) holds lava lakes; recorded games found a usable pool within minutes of reaching y-45 in 2 of 6 descents and saw 1 usable pool in ~29 hours of time above y-20. A frame needs a water bucket to cast and a light (flint and steel; flint from gravel, which lies at every depth). Now: iron pickaxe, water bucket, 2 cooked beef, no flint; y-45 in a staircase descent, stalled for 90 s; no lava seen or heard yet. Good: keep going down to the y-50s or, already there, search at that depth: tunnel or walk toward an open cave, a cave opening, or lava heard popping, staying near the lava level; filling the water bucket at aquifer water met on the way is fine. Bad: climbing back to the surface or above y-20, leaving for food while cooked food is held, a long tunnel at the current height away from the floors, or idling. Neutral: reads, memory notes or tool selection alone; when they precede a world action, program or intent in the same answer, grade that action or intent. An intent (taskPlan) counts by what it commits to. An immediate threat (hostile in reach, lava contact, low health, drowning, night mob in reach) takes priority and handling it is good. Do not assume unobserved caves, ores or lava.
